subject: DPF, KMS custody & DPA annex — transfer assurance for EuroBank RFI
messages:
From: Olivia Baxter <olivia.baxter@eurobank.com>

Cc: Jules Martin <jules.martin@eurobank.com>, EuroBank Legal <legal@eurobank.com>

Subject: RFI: transfer assurance and KMS custody — follow-up questions

Avery — thanks for the overview call earlier. As part of our procurement RFI we need concise, evidence-backed answers on two combined topics so we can move to legal review: (1) which cross-border transfer mechanisms Redwood intends to rely on for EU personal data exported to the US and APAC; and (2) how your KMS/HSM custody model works for customer-controlled keys (BYOK) and auditability.

Specifically: 
- Please confirm whether Redwood is relying on the EU-US Data Privacy Framework (DPF), Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs), or a hybrid approach in the current DPA annex. If hybrid, list fallback order.
- For DPF: do you maintain certification scope that covers inference telemetry/logs and pseudonymised training/telemetry data?
- For BYOK: can customers bring keys stored in their own cloud KMS (AWS KMS / Google Cloud KMS) and have Redwood never persist plaintext keys? If yes, describe key rotation and emergency key-revocation procedures.
- For audits: what evidence (logs, attestations) will you provide for cross-border access requests and routing decisions?

We referenced the partial draft DPA annex you uploaded to the portal. If you can provide a short written response and the updated annex (tracked changes preferred) by end of day Thursday that would be extremely helpful.

Best,
Olivia Baxter
Head of Vendor Risk — EuroBank

(Attachment: eurobank_rfi_questions.xlsx (spreadsheet stub))

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary up front: Redwood's primary transfer mechanism for EU-origin personal data is the EU-US Data Privacy Framework where applicable, supplemented by Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) for jurisdictions or use-cases outside the DPF scope; our DPA annex includes explicit fallback order and operational controls. We can support customer-controlled KMS (BYOK) with an HSM-backed gateway and we do not persist plaintext customer keys.

I'll attach an updated DPA annex (v2) and a short control matrix answering each RFI line-by-line. Marissa (security/compliance) and Ben (product) are looped in for the technical details below. We'll get a tracked-changes PDF into the drive and send a signatures/DocuSign link if legal is comfortable.

Next steps: we will send a detailed technical reply in one follow-up email within 48 hours, plus the annex and key-flow diagram.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: RFI: transfer assurance and KMS custody — follow-up questions

Jules / Olivia — thanks for the follow-ups. Below is a concise mapping and the operational details you requested. See attached control matrix and key-flow diagram for visuals. I've numbered answers to match your points.

1) Transfer mechanisms & fallback order- Primary: EU–US Data Privacy Framework (DPF) — Redwood maintains an active DPF certification that covers processing of customer-provided inference payloads, service logs needed for debugging (pseudonymised), and telemetry used for performance monitoring.
- Secondary / fallback: Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) (2021 Annex) are embedded in our DPA annex for customers who require contractual safeguards or where DPF does not apply (e.g., transfers to APAC regions without an adequacy decision).
- Tertiary: Where neither DPF nor SCCs are sufficient for a specific country, we offer per-customer contractual addenda and localized deployment options (VPC private deployment or EU-only Dedicated pools).

2) DPF scope detail (mapping to your appendix A)- Inference request payloads (text prompts and structured inputs): INCLUDED- Model response tokens (outputs to customer): INCLUDED- Real-time operational logs (errors, latencies) that are pseudonymised or are aggregated: INCLUDED- Persistent training/labeling datasets: NOT INCLUDED in DPF scope unless the customer explicitly opts-in for model fine-tuning; we treat fine-tuning data under a separate agreement and explicit consent flow.

3) KMS / BYOK cryptographic flow (AWS KMS example)- Customer stores a key in their AWS KMS (symmetric key) and grants Redwood a limited-use KMS-Decrypt or KMS-GenerateDataKey permissions scoped to a short-lived envelope key operation.
- Redwood requests an encrypted data key (GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext or Encrypt) from the customer's KMS; the plaintext key material never leaves the customer's KMS.
- Redwood uses the encrypted data key as an envelope key; decryption occurs inside a transient HSM-backed execution environment on our side where plaintext is kept in memory for the minimal lifetime of the inference call and never persisted to disk. Memory is zeroed on process teardown.
- Key rotation: customer rotates in their cloud KMS per their policy; Redwood supports key-identifier updates with no service interruption using per-transaction key metadata.
- Emergency revocation: customer can revoke KMS permissions or rotate keys. Once revoked, subsequent calls fail fast; we also run an emergency purge to drop any in-memory references and provide audit entries showing the refusal of further decrypt attempts.

4) Auditability & evidence- We provide: immutable access logs (request id, timestamp, decision, routing node id), KMS operation logs (references to the KMS operation id), and cryptographic key identifiers (key id fingerprint) as part of the evidence package.
- For high-assurance customers we can supply: time-limited access to a read-only audit bundle (S3 link) containing redacted logs, a compliance summary report, and our SOC 2 Type II attestation.

5) EU-residency routing option- Yes. For customers on Dedicated or Private deployments we can route inference to EU-only serving pools. For Hosted customers we offer a regional routing policy: EU-only processing is available via an opt-in configuration (may add latency vs. multi-region failover and can affect caching economics). This is documented in the DPA annex section 4.3.

Attachments included: redwood_dpa_annex_v2.pdf (tracked), crossborder_control_matrix.xlsx (mapping), kms_key_flow_diagram.png (flow).
